actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

dimensions.assessment: Affects copyright owners, foreign website operators, large broadband internet service providers, public domain name resolution services, and internet users in the United States.
dimensions.evidence: direct service providers to take reasonable measures to prevent users in the United States from using the system or network of those service providers to access the foreign digital piracy site

dimensions.assessment: Imposes significant operational requirements on major internet service providers to block specific foreign sites and grants extensive immunity provisions.
dimensions.evidence: A service provider subject to an order issued under subsection (c) shall be immune from liability for any injury alleged... as a result of a measure... taken in good faith

dimensions.assessment: Permits service providers to seek reimbursement from petitioners for reasonable costs directly incurred to comply with blocking orders, excluding capital expenditures.
dimensions.evidence: the court may order the petitioner that sought the order to pay reasonable costs directly incurred by the service provider to comply with the order.

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title 17 of the U.S. Code to establish a brand new judicial mechanism for designating foreign piracy sites and issuing network-blocking orders.
dimensions.evidence: Chapter 5 of title 17, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 502 the following: Sec. 502A.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory procedures with individual site designation orders expiring after 360 days unless extended or unless a subsequent order is sought.
dimensions.evidence: an order to designate a foreign online location as a foreign digital piracy site under this subsection shall expire... on the date that is 360 days after the date on which the court issues the order

missing_information: Estimates of court caseloads and administrative burdens on federal district courts.
importance_detail.rationale: Amends copyright law to allow owners and exclusive licensees of exclusive rights to petition federal district courts for orders designating foreign online locations as digital piracy sites and directing domestic broadband and domain name providers to block access.
